Specialty chemicals manufacturing facility on Jurong Island up for sale by private treaty
article:
A speciality chemicals manufacturing facility on Jurong Island is up for sale by private treaty.

Located at 33 Ayer Merbau Road, the industrial asset comprises an open-structure process plant; a single-storey technical building with a laboratory and control room; and a two-storey office building with offices, meeting rooms and staff facilities.

No guide price has been disclosed for the asset, with marketing agent CBRE stating that the seller is “open to considering any reasonable offers that may be put forward”.

The facility occupies 278,000 sq ft of land zoned for Business 2 use. It currently has a total gross floor area (GFA) of about 25,730 sq ft, which is materially below the site’s maximum allowable GFA of 278,000 sq ft, based on its permissible plot ratio of 1.0. This provides “substantial future expansion potential”, CBRE said in an Oct 19 release.

Located on the Jurong Island energy and petrochemical hub, the facility was originally configured for alkoxylation and surfactant production. It has since been fully decommissioned and decontaminated.

The asset can be repurposed for a broad range of chemical, specialty materials and advanced manufacturing applications.

“The property's existing process infrastructure, utility connections and significant expansion potential offer purchasers a faster route to market compared to developing a new facility from the ground up,” said Graeme Bolin, CBRE’s head of occupier and leasing for industrial and logistics services.

He added that the facility’s fully decommissioned and decontaminated status will allow purchasers to expedite future production plans.

title: 5 Best Blue-Chip Stocks Offering a Safe Haven for Income Seekers
article:
When markets get choppy, investors wonder where their money is safest.
They tend to turn to
blue chips
, which have proven business models, strong balance sheets and established dividend payout policies.
But “blue chip” doesn’t automatically mean safe, and a
high yield
can be a warning sign.
What matters is whether a company can keep generating cash and paying
dividends
through the cycle.
We examine five Singapore blue-chip names through this lens.
What Makes a Blue Chip a Potential Safe Haven for Income?
Earnings should hold up through the cycle.
Dividends should be funded by recurring cash flow, not borrowing.
The balance sheet should be able to fund future growth or cushion downturns.
There should be a strong track record of growing or maintaining payouts.
Valuation has to be reasonable, because even a great company is a poor investment if you overpay.
DBS Group Holdings Ltd (SGX: D05): The Banking Blue Chip
DBS is Singapore’s largest bank, with retail, wealth and institutional franchises across 19 global markets.
Net profit hit a record S$3.08 billion in the second quarter of 2026, up 9%, even as its net interest margin (NIM) compressed to 1.87% from 2.05% a year earlier on rate cuts.
Wealth management, treasury, and markets trading all posted double-digit growth, keeping return on equity (ROE) at 17.9% and the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio steady at 1.0%.
Wealth assets under management (AUM) crossed the half-trillion mark, and management aims to grow wealth AUM to more than S$1 trillion by 2030.
Its Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio stood at 16.6%, backing the capital return dividend on top of the ordinary dividend.
DBS is not fully shielded from an economic slowdown: slower loan growth, rising credit losses could weigh on profit, while further rate cuts could squeeze margins.
Related articles:
DBS, OCBC, UOB: Singapore Banks Are Cheaper, But Are They a Bargain?
DBS at a Record High: Buy, Hold or Wait for a Pullback?
Sheng Siong Group Ltd (SGX: OV8): The Defensive Consumer Blue Chip
Sheng Siong is Singapore’s third-largest supermarket chain and enjoys recurring demand for essential products.
In 1H2026, revenue rose 11.9% to S$855.4 million and net profit climbed 11.9% to S$81.0 million.
Comparable-store sales alone grew 3.3%, and gross margin improved to 31.8% from 30.8% even as staff costs rose.
The FY2025 payout ratio was 70.4% of net profit, and operating cash flow was S$236.6 million, up 8.1%.
Three new stores opened this quarter, and a S$520 million distribution centre at Sungei Kadut, designed to serve more than 120 stores, should be completed by 2029.
Key risks include rising input costs, weaker consumer demand and more intense competition, which could squeeze margins.
Related articles:
The S$520M Roadmap: Inside Sheng Siong’s Next Phase of Expansion
From Costco to Sheng Siong: Analysing the Consumer Staples Moat Across Two Markets
Singapore Technologies Engineering Ltd (SGX: S63), or ST Engineering: The Industrial Blue Chip
ST Engineering builds satellites, services aircraft and runs smart-city and defence systems.
The company’s business is based on recurring services and long-term contracts on infrastructure.
1H2026 revenue rose 11% to S$6.57 billion, and net profit jumped 27% to S$512 million as profits grew faster than revenue.
The real growth driver is the order book, which hit a record S$35.7 billion, with S$5.7 billion due for delivery by year-end.
Operating cash flow rose 26% to S$960 million, funding ordinary dividends that have climbed from S$0.15 in FY2021 to S$0.18 in FY2025.
A further 5-cent special dividend lifted the FY2025 total to S$0.23.
As at 30 June 2026, net debt stood at about S$4.4 billion, manageable against cash generation.
It is imperative for ST Engineering to execute well and operate within budget across a backlog this large.
Related articles:
Why Has ST Engineering Become So Much More Valuable? We Went Back Through 10 Years of Results
Yangzijiang vs ST Engineering: Which Singapore Growth Stock Would I Buy?
Singapore Telecommunications Limited (SGX: Z74), or Singtel: The Telecommunications Blue Chip
Singtel is Singapore’s largest telco, with 839 million mobile customers across the group and its associates.
Mobile phone and broadband plans are essentials and are less affected by economic cycles.
Revenue was little changed at S$14.26 billion in FY2026 and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) edged up 1.5% to S$3.85 billion.
Underlying net profit rose 12% to S$2.77 billion and free cash flow was S$2.44 billion.
The core dividend takes 80% of underlying profit, and asset sales fund a further value realisation payout: about S$5.8 billion of the S$9 billion capital recycling target has been completed
The higher-margin push is data centres, with Digital InfraCo revenue up 26%, while capital spending is set to climb from S$2.48 billion to about S$3.0 billion in FY2027.
Related articles:
DBS, Singtel and ST Engineering Have Rallied: Which Is Still Worth Buying?
Singtel vs ST Engineering: Which Dividend Stock Is Better for the Next 10 Years?
Singapore Exchange Limited (SGX: S68), or SGX: The Financial Exchange Blue Chip
SGX is Singapore’s only exchange operator and runs an asset-light business model.
FY2026 net revenue rose 13.9% to S$1.48 billion, and adjusted net profit climbed 24.6% to S$759.5 million, a 51.4% margin.
Volumes did the work: securities daily average value hit S$1.8 billion, up 35%, and currency derivatives volumes rose 31%.
New products are widening the base, from Asian government bond futures to over-the-counter gold clearing and crypto perpetual futures.
SGX plans about S$100 million of capital spending in FY2027, including next-generation trading systems.
However, it’s still a volume business, so quieter markets would hurt revenue and profit.

Each stock plays a different role in your portfolio: DBS acts as the income anchor, Sheng Siong the defensive holding, ST Engineering the dividend grower, Singtel the recurring cash-flow play and SGX the diversification play.
Are Blue Chips Really a “Safe Haven”?
Not entirely.
Blue chips can still fall sharply in a sell-off, and dividends aren’t guaranteed.
Strong companies have earnings downturns too, and a rich valuation makes any fall worse.
Income investors can assess these stocks by asking a few simple questions.
Start with the dividend: Is the payout growing or sustainable?
Then check whether earnings and cash flows can hold up when conditions get worse.
Look at the balance sheet next: Can the company withstand a downturn without cutting its payout?
Finally, check valuations to see whether the good news has already been priced in.
Get Smart: Look for Resilience, Not Just Yield
Blue chips can anchor an income portfolio, but they don’t all offer the same earnings resilience or dividend durability.
Judge each one not by yield alone but by its cash generation, balance sheet, dividend record and valuation.
Income investing is about owning businesses that keep generating cash in all market conditions, because sustainable cash flow is what pays the dividend.

title: JPMorgan and Alibaba are said among investors in Dongshan’s listing — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 19): JPMorgan Chase & Co’s asset management arm and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd are set to be among cornerstone investors in printed circuit board maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co’s upcoming Hong Kong listing, according to people familiar with the matter.

CPE, formerly known as Citic PE, and Montage Technology Co are also planning to participate as cornerstone investors, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing confidential information.

Dongshan Precision is planning to start taking orders as soon as Tuesday for its share sale that could raise as much as US$1.8 billion, including a greenshoe option, the people said. The cornerstone investors are expected to take up about half of the deal, they said.

Deliberations are ongoing and details including cornerstone lineup, size and timing of the offering may change.

Representatives for Dongshan Precision and JPMorgan Asset Management declined to comment, while Alibaba, CPE and Montage didn’t immediately respond to requests seeking comment.

Dongshan Precision’s listing builds on a record summer for Hong Kong, which is en route to overtake 2021 in annual proceeds from share sales, in large part thanks to jumbo offerings by companies along the artificial intelligence supply chain.

See also: Dubai sweetens first IPO since war with US$592 mil dividend

Other PCB makers which tapped the market this year include Victory Giant Technology Huizhou Co, which raised US$3 billion in one of Hong Kong’s biggest deals of the year, and Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic Co, which completed a US$650 million debut last month.

However, Dongshan Precision is braving the market as investors have become increasingly concerned about the levels of AI spending and how it’s being financed at a time of rising yields.

Earlier this month, US semiconductor shares suffered an eight-session rout — the longest since 2008 — that wiped roughly 16% off the sector’s benchmark, while the Nasdaq 100 experienced its worst week since April 2025.

See also: Mi Material launches IPO at $1.80 each, aims to raise gross proceeds of $168.2 mil

That negative sentiment has started to have ripple effects on initial public offerings. Australian data center company Firmus Grid Ltd pulled its roughly US$5 billion IPO when investors balked at the valuation it sought, while AirTrunk, which also operates data centers, pushed back a planned real estate investment trust IPO in Singapore to next year.

Dongshan Precision, which already trades in Shenzhen, has lost more than half its value since a peak in June, giving it a market capitalisation of 224 billion yuan (RM136.7 billion). The Suzhou-based firm makes PCBs as well as optical transceivers, critical components for AI.

UBS Group AG, Guotai Haitong Securities Co, GF Securities Co and Citic Securities Co are joint sponsors for the Hong Kong listing, according to a preliminary prospectus.

title: China's overnight rate set to become main policy benchmark
article:
(Oct 19): China’s central bank signalled its overnight reverse repurchase rate will replace the current seven-day rate as the new policy benchmark, in another step that aligns it closer with global peers.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) will study the possibility of switching the main tenor of its open market operations to the overnight one at an appropriate time, and the overnight reverse repo rate will then become the main policy rate, Pan Gongsheng, the governor of the PBOC, said at the Financial Street Forum in Beijing on Monday, according to local media outlet Cailian.

Overnight repos are the most heavily traded product in the interbank money market and their rate, known as DR001, has already become the target of the PBOC’s operations, Cailian cited Pan as saying. Aligning the tenor of central bank operations with the target would make the PBOC’s guidance more precise, he was cited as saying.

The overnight repo rate was steady at 1.26% following the news. The yuan rose 0.1% to 6.6813 per dollar in the offshore market, holding on to an earlier gain. Yields on the government’s 10-year and 30-year bonds were little changed at 1.64% and 2.06% respectively.

The PBOC first introduced an overnight tenor to its open market operations in June in a key move to expand its short-term liquidity toolkit. The decision has fuelled speculation that the overnight rate will play a greater role and eventually become the main policy benchmark to anchor market borrowing costs.

Such an approach would make the PBOC operate more like other major central banks, which tend to treat overnight market rates as the main target of policy operations.

See also: China’s growth rebound tops forecasts to close in on target

The costs of overnight borrowing among banks have dropped below 1.3% in October to their lowest level since May, widening their gap against the seven-day reverse repo rate — which the PBOC has at 1.4%. In June, the PBOC set the rate on the new overnight reverse repo tool at 1.25%, Bloomberg News reported previously.

The recent declines in market rates reflect expectations of a transition in China’s monetary policy anchor, according to analysts.

The central bank has conducted overnight reverse repurchase operations every month from June to September, and their frequency as well as volume offered have been on the rise. The operations have helped address market demand for funds during month-end payments or tax payment times.

title: Samsung, SK Hynix slide causes US$137 bil South Korean pension hit
article:
(Oct 19): South Korea’s main pension fund took a 182 trillion won (US$137 billion or $175 billion) hit after a decline in stakes of equities including Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc.

The estimated value of the National Pension Service (NPS) stakes of 5% or more in 287 listed companies fell to 333.53 trillion won as of Oct 15 from 515.93 trillion won at the end of June, according to financial data provider FnGuide. It was the first quarterly decline since the fourth quarter of 2024, based on the NPS’ past performance, and marks a dramatic reversal for a fund that posted record-breaking returns in the first half.

The reversal underscores the vulnerability of one of the world’s largest pension funds to swings in its home market, where its enormous holdings in chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix leave it particularly exposed to the boom-and-bust cycle in technology stocks.

The decline contrasts sharply with the NPS’ performance in the first half, when it reported a 27.2% return, its best performance for the period since at least 2022. The NPS had 1,866 trillion won under management at of the end of June.

The NPS hasn’t reported the third-quarter performance yet, a spokesperson for the fund said in a text message.

The fund raised its year-end target allocation to South Korean equities in May while lowering its target exposure to foreign equities, increasing its planned exposure to a market that has been one of the world’s best performers in the first half.

See also: Meta says Claude AI tool triggered No Kings Instagram suspension

SK Hynix accounted for the largest decline, with the value of the NPS’ holdings in the chipmaker falling by about 74.2 trillion won. Its Samsung Electronics holdings lost about 56.9 trillion won in value. The two stocks accounted for about 72% of the total decline.

South Korean stocks have been whipsawed in recent months amid the introduction of single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds and mounting questions over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence-driven rally. South Korea’s Kospi index hit a record closing high of 9,114.55 on June 22, before falling about 39% by Oct 15. The NPS’ stake in SK Hynix declined to 7.32% from 7.5%, while its stake in Samsung Electronics remained unchanged at 7.84%.

The market decline has also drawn the NPS into a political debate over whether the pension giant should do more to cushion sharp swings in South Korean equities.

See also: China’s CXMT swings to profit after memory chip prices surge

The opposition People Power Party has criticised the NPS for failing to act as a market stabiliser during the recent sell-off, arguing that its decision to suspend rebalancing earlier this year left it with less room to buy stocks as the market fell.
